messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran the INT8/GPTQ bakeoff for the new-3B bring-up. seeing sporadic activation surges concentrated in attention projection out (attn.proj_out) around layers 14-17. quality delta on our LLaMAEval set is bad (3-4% EM drop) with default GPTQ flow.

oana: can you paste the per-layer summary? a short table is fine.

maya: here’s the abbreviated scan (sample 2k prompts):
```
layer,max_act,99.9pct,kurtosis,channels_high
13,7.2,4.1,15.2,3
14,18.9,12.3,62.8,2
15,22.4,14.8,110.1,4  <-- huge spike
16,16.0,10.2,40.7,1
17,9.8,6.0,22.9,2
```
comments: spikes are highly channel-localized (1-4 channels), massive long tails.

kevin: classic outlier channels. did you try per-channel rescale or surgical clamp? skipping layer quantization might be easiest fallback.

maya: ran three quick variants:
- baseline: GPTQ int4 (all layers quantized) -> +3.9% EM drop
- variant A: skip quant for layers 14-17 (float fallback) -> +1.1% EM drop, +0.9ms median latency
- variant B: per-channel median scaling + top-channel clamp (scale factor 1.6, clamp top1 to 2.5*sigma) -> +0.6% EM drop, +4% throughput loss (kernel overhead)

eval-bot: evaluation summary attached: {"baseline_em_delta":"+3.9%","skip_layers_em_delta":"+1.1%","pc_scale_clamp_em_delta":"+0.6%","latency_p50_change":"+0.9ms/+4%"} :white_check_mark:

srinivas: notes on tradeoffs — skip-layers reduces regression but increases memory usage (float weights). per-channel scaling keeps memory low but needs new kernel path (AWQ-like) and may cost compute. both valid deployment profiles.

ravi: also watch KV-cache alignment: if you run mixed quant/float layers some kernels expect different kv packing. pin model version and seqlen in the infra rollout.

oana: could we automate detection? proposal: run a cheap per-channel 99.9pct sweep on a 256-prompt sample during onboarding, flag layers with >3x median(99.9pct) and >kurtosis threshold 30. auto-suggest either skip-layer or pc-scale+clamp.

maya: implemented a quick scanner script and a one-liner to generate candidate config:
```
# scan
python tools/scan_activations.py --model ./checkpoints/new-3B --sample 256 --metric 99.9 --out scan.json
# generate config from scan.json (pseudo)
python tools/gen_quant_profile.py --scan scan.json --strategy auto_surgical > quant_profile.yaml
```
summary of generated entries:
```
- skip_layers: [14,15]
- pc_scaling:
  layer: 16
  scale: 1.6
  clamp_topk: 1
  clamp_mult: 2.5
```

kevin: nice. i’ll queue a longer-run (1000 prompts) with both profiles and AWQ fallback. can we tag experiments so infra routes to dedicated GPU pool?

srinivas: for rollout, recommend two named variants: `conservative-surge-safe` (skip-layers float fallback) and `aggressive-surge-opt` (pc-scale+clamp). route 5-10% traffic to aggressive, monitor eval-suite EM and embedding drift. set automatic rollback at >0.5% EM regression for 1h.

maya: added these as candidate model variants in the onboarding PR draft. also logging suggestions: add per-request \"activation-surge\" boolean if any flagged channel > threshold, so we can alert in console.

oana: for the automation threshold, i'd add an exponential backoff: if a layer is flagged in >3 onboarding runs then default to skip-layer to be conservative.

ravi: small infra checklist before rollout:
- pin quant kernel ABI in runtime metadata
- ensure model shard alignment for mixed precision
- include fallback route to float-hosted variant

kevin: starting the longer queue now. will report back with eval-bot JSON. :rocket:

maya: thanks — once we have the 1k-run numbers we'll pick a default for Hosted and a Dedicated reserved template. opening the PR with scan + two profiles after kevin posts results. :thumbsup:

(threads: short follow-ups to add logs and PR link will follow)
